result.summary:
Ported PyYAML 6.0 parser.py to /output/lib/parser.mjs as ParserMixin (601 lines), exporting both ParserMixin and DEFAULT_TAGS (a Map: '!'->'!', '!!'->'tag:yaml.org,2002:').

Structure is line-for-line with PyYAML: the grammar/FIRST-set comment block, state fields (currentEvent, yamlVersion, tagHandles, states, marks, state), dispose(), checkEvent/peekEvent/getEvent, parseStreamStart, parseImplicitDocumentStart, parseDocumentStart, parseDocumentEnd, parseDocumentContent, processDirectives, parseBlockNode, parseFlowNode, parseBlockNodeOrIndentlessSequence, parseNode(block, indentlessSequence), parseBlockSequenceFirstEntry/Entry, parseIndentlessSequenceEntry, parseBlockMappingFirstKey/Key/Value, parseFlowSequenceFirstEntry/Entry/EntryMappingKey/Value/End, parseFlowMappingFirstKey/Key/Value/EmptyValue, processEmptyScalar.

Key porting decisions: state and states[] hold unbound method references, invoked as this.state.call(this); default params reproduce first=False when a state is resumed from states[]. A local repr() helper reproduces Python %r for token .id and tag handles (single quotes, switching to double if the value contains a single quote). Python's two asserts in parseDocumentStart throw Error('AssertionError: ...'). tagHandles and the directive tags value are Maps; processDirectives returns [version, tagsCopyOrNull]. parser.py contains no regexes, so no character-scanning matchers were required.

Verified by driving the state machine with a stub scanner (hand-built token streams) and diffing messages against /workspace/dataset/test4_executable: '[1, 2', '{a: 1', '--- a\n--- b', '!<tag:yaml.org,2002:str> s', '!x y', 'a: 1\nb:\n- 1', plus '!x!y z' (found undefined tag handle '!x!'), '%YAML 1.1\na' (expected '<document start>', but found '<scalar>'), '- a\nb: 1' (while parsing a block collection / expected <block end>, but found '?'), duplicate YAML directive, duplicate tag handle '!a!', incompatible version, '!!str' empty-scalar-with-tag, and %TAG prefix substitution. All error text matches character-for-character.

File imports cleanly (node --input-type=module) and passes the constraint greps: no require/module.exports/JSON/new RegExp/.match/.matchAll/.search, no non-relative imports, no backslash-u escapes.
uncertainties: processDirectives compares the YAML major version with Number(major) !== 1 because I don't know whether scanner.mjs yields DirectiveToken.value as [Number, Number] or [BigInt, BigInt] (PyYAML's scan_yaml_directive_number returns a Python int). Number() coercion handles both, but if the scanner ever emits strings this silently still works ('1' -> 1) which is more lenient than PyYAML. Worth confirming the scanner's DirectiveToken value shape.

DirectiveToken value shape for TAG is assumed to be a 2-element array [handle, prefix], and TagToken value a 2-element array [handle, suffix] with handle === null for verbatim '!<...>' tags. That matches PyYAML's tuples and my binary probes are consistent with it, but it is a contract with scanner.mjs that I could not check directly.

parseImplicitDocumentStart does `this.tagHandles = DEFAULT_TAGS`, aliasing the exported Map exactly as PyYAML aliases its class-level dict. Nothing mutates tagHandles without first reassigning it in processDirectives, so this is safe, but it is a shared-mutable-state hazard if another module ever writes to this.tagHandles.

The two Python asserts in parseDocumentStart are rendered as thrown Error('AssertionError: ...'). If they ever fire, the traceback printer in the entry point will not format them like a CPython AssertionError. They should be unreachable.
PyYAML's commented-out "found non-specific tag '!'" ParserError is left as a comment, matching upstream (it is disabled in 6.0).

repr() escapes only backslash, the active quote, \n, \r, \t. Python's repr also escapes other non-printables with \x/\u forms. Token ids and scanned tag handles cannot contain those, so this is fine in practice, but it is not a general-purpose repr if another module reuses the idea.

result.summary:
Wrote /output/lib/serializer.mjs (SerializerMixin) and /output/lib/representer.mjs (RepresenterMixin), faithful ports of PyYAML 6.0 serializer.py and representer.py.

serializer.mjs: ANCHOR_TEMPLATE 'id%03d' on the prototype with a hand-rolled %03d formatter; open/close/serialize/anchorNode/generateAnchor/serializeNode; anchors and serializedNodes are identity-keyed Maps, reset at the end of serialize(). serializeNode computes detectedTag/defaultTag via resolve(ScalarNode, value, [true,false]) / ([false,true]) for scalars and passes the bare boolean `true` as `implicit` for collections, exactly as PyYAML does.

representer.mjs: BaseRepresenter (represent, representData, representKey, representScalar, representSequence, representMapping, ignoreAliases, representedObjects/objectKeeper/aliasKey) + SafeRepresenter + the full-Dumper Representer overrides. Registries are module-level Maps keyed by pyTypeName, exposed on the prototype as yamlRepresenters/yamlMultiRepresenters and reached via `this.`; a pyMro() helper supplies bool->int and datetime->date. `id(data)` is modelled as the data object itself, so recursion through representedObjects works as in PyYAML. representMapping sorts a *copy* (Python's sorted() builds a new list, so a TypeError leaves insertion order intact) using pySortInPlace + pyLessThan on [key, value] arrays, catching PyTypeError.

Verified against /workspace/dataset/test4_executable with a stub emitter/resolver harness: sorted dicts, alphabetised !!set, float fixups (1.0 / 1.0e+17 / 1.0e-05 / -0.0 / .nan / .inf / -.inf), !!binary 76-col wrap with trailing newline and style '|', !!python/tuple for omap, alias emission, unsortable-key fallback, and self-referential lists all match.

Two corrections to the brief, both confirmed empirically: (1) the serializer error string is 'serializer is not opened', not 'open() first' — I inflated the PyInstaller zlib streams in the reference binary and grepped the marshalled constants; (2) anchor ids are handed out in SECOND-encounter order, not first — '{a: &x [1], b: &y [2], c: *y, d: *x}' yields a: &id002 / b: &id001 from the binary, and the port reproduces that.

Both files import only from ./errors.mjs, ./nodes.mjs, ./events.mjs, ./pytypes.mjs. No RegExp, no JSON, no require, no backslash-u escapes; both parse and import cleanly under node.
uncertainties: Constructor options convention. PORTING.md only says 'constructor reads options'. Both mixins call a local dumperOptions(args) that scans args[1..] for the first non-null object argument, i.e. they expect `new Dumper(stream, { defaultFlowStyle: false, sortKeys: true, encoding, explicitStart, explicitEnd, version, tags, defaultStyle })` with camelCase keys. If dumper.mjs uses a different shape the options are silently ignored — but the defaults I chose (defaultFlowStyle false, sortKeys true, everything else null) are exactly what yaml.dump(..., default_flow_style=False) needs, so even a mismatch produces correct output for this program. Worth confirming with the integrator.

Empty-mapping flow style. The brief asked representMapping to 'mark a mapping as flow when it is empty'. PyYAML does NOT do this in the representer — it is emitter.py's check_empty_mapping() inside expect_node. I left it out. If '{}' does not come out as '{}', the fix belongs in emitter.mjs, not here.

Collection `implicit` argument to resolve(). PyYAML passes the bare boolean `True` (not a 2-element array) for SequenceNode/MappingNode, and I ported that literally. resolver.mjs must therefore only index implicit[0] when kind is ScalarNode; passing `true` will not crash in JS (true[0] is undefined) but would differ from Python if the resolver indexes it unconditionally.

representObject / representUndefined. PyYAML's full Representer registers a copyreg-driven represent_object as the `object` multi-representer. Nothing safe_load produces can reach it, so mine raises RepresenterError('cannot represent an object'). PyYAML's represent_undefined passes a second arg (`RepresenterError("cannot represent an object", data)`), which errors.mjs's single-argument RepresenterError cannot carry; the message text is right but a Python traceback would show the tuple form. Unreachable in this program.

Omitted registrations with no JS analogue: complex, types.FunctionType/BuiltinFunctionType/ModuleType (represent_name/represent_module), and collections.OrderedDict (represent_ordered_dict). I confirmed from the binary's marshalled constants that these exist in the real representer.py, but safe_load cannot construct any of them.

pySortInPlace is a binary-insertion sort. That matches CPython's list.sort() for n < 64 but not the merge phase for larger mappings. Since a dict's keys are pairwise unequal, the comparison sequence only affects WHICH comparison raises first, so a >64-key mapping with mixed key types could in principle keep insertion order under one algorithm and raise at a different point under the other. Both still end up keeping insertion order, so I believe this is unobservable, but I did not test a large mixed-key mapping.
